messages:
alex: ran nsys on dedicate-prod-3 with a long-seq load (seq len 4k -> 16k). timeline looks fragmented, lots of tiny kernels during KV access phase. posting the nsys top-kern summary I pasted below.

alex: nsys summary (top kernels by total time):
```
kernel_name, calls, total_ms, pct_time, avg_sm_util
kv_lookup_v2, 12456, 412.3, 28.7, 14
batch_coalesce_kernel, 9820, 173.5, 12.1, 22
attn_kv_update, 842, 158.2, 11.0, 36
triton_gemm_fp16, 310, 129.6, 9.0, 78
prefix_cache_hop, 24000, 118.7, 8.3, 8
kv_prefetch_kern, 11600, 96.2, 6.7, 11
softmax_cuda, 620, 82.1, 5.7, 65
reduce_sum, 12440, 62.0, 4.3, 9
kv_evict_scan, 1100, 44.9, 3.1, 18
other_small_kernels, 45000, 202.0, 14.0, 10
```

alex: TL;DR: top two by wall time are kv_lookup_v2 and a ton of tiny prefix/cache hops. avg SM util is very low on those which suggests launch/overhead+warp underutil.

maria: which commit + config? did we enable the new micro-batch coalescer last week?

alex: main @ 3f9b2d7 + micro-coalesce enabled with threshold 4. Sequence distro has heavy variance so coalescer is emitting many small groups.

jin: ok that explains it. many tiny launches -> kernel launch overhead dominates and prevents high occupancy. also KV lookup has lock-step divergence because some threads hit cache miss and do extra work -> warp imbalance.

sam: do we have perfetto timeline? visual helps.

alex: perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/r/abcd1234 (private). screenshot: you can see repeated spikes ~150-300us separated by gaps ~100-200us during KV phase.

perf-bot: Perf alert: 2.3% median p90 latency regression on main in last deploy (detected by nightly job).

lina: quick triage checklist: 
- try increasing micro-coalesce threshold to 16 for long-seq workloads
- switch KV lookup path to fused_kv_lookup (fewer kernel launches, trades memory)
- enable kv_prefetch_kern earlier to hide mem latency
- consider cudaGraph capture for repeated tiny kernels

lina: config snippet to flip for an experiment:
```json
{"batching": {"micro_coalesce_threshold": 16, "enable_fused_kv": true, "use_cuda_graphs": true}}
```

maria: I'll spin a local repro with synthetic seq-distro and run nsys + perfetto. will capture kernel-by-call latency distribution and per-kernel SM occupancy.

jin: for kernel ranking I'd like to compute a simple priority score = total_ms * (1 + (1 - avg_sm_util/100)) * log(1 + calls). That will push up long-running low-occupancy kernels and high-call-count tiny kernels.

alex: sounds good. can you output top-10 by that score and attach to the issue?

sam: small note: if fused_kv_lookup increases memory pressure we might see downstream cache evictions; add a kv_evict_scan monitor.

alex: assigning: jin -> kernel improvements (fused kernel prototype), sam -> batching heuristics and cudaGraph experiment, maria -> repro + traces, lina -> perf regression dashboard & alert tuning. I'll open an issue with the nsys summary and timeline links. :thumbsup:

maria: will post initial repro by EOD and link traces in the issue.

jin: quick thought — also measure launch-to-launch gap on timeline; if >50us we're definitely launch-bound and cudaGraph is the fastest win.

alex: agreed. thanks everyone.
